_comment: Article's language experiment (claims 19-20) on Zucchet et al.'s synthetic biographies with a small Gemma 3 style decoder (rcdl/bios.py): d = 256, 6 layers (5 local : 1 global), 4 query heads and 1 KV head of width 64, GeGLU width 1,024, tied embeddings. Batch 64 x 512 tokens (about 320 biographies per step), 6,000 steps, AdamW 4e-4 with betas 0.9 / 0.95, weight decay 0.1, cosine to 1e-7 (Zucchet et al. defaults). A: plateau against the number of individuals N (GeGLU; N = 8,192 is the C run). S: growing-RBF kernel width scan at N = 4,096. B and C at N = 8,192: Cos-Bochner throughout at widths 1k / 4k / 16k, Cos-Bochner 64k in the last layer, growing RBF and the routed-GeGLU control in the last layer; C runs then fine-tune on 1,024 new individuals for 1,000 steps at constant lr 3e-5 without replay (Zucchet et al. Sec. 4), and one GeGLU run with 50% replay. Growing RBF tables: 8M rows (ring buffer) for fine-tuning runs, so that rows of the last ~1,000 pre-training steps survive the 1,000 fine-tuning steps.
